signal: Prove launched its Identity Platform as the trust layer for an agentic world and raised $40M led by MassMutual Ventures and Capital One Ventures

email.body1:
Michael, saw Prove launched its Identity Platform for the agentic world and pulled in $40M from MassMutual and Capital One Ventures.

That kind of platform shift usually creates more in-market accounts than an SDR team can personally touch, so reps end up buried in research and CRM instead of conversations. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, which lifts each rep to 3-5x more meetings without new headcount.

I built a personalized signal play for Prove off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.subject2: three drafts for your top accounts
email.body2:
Michael, quick follow-up for Prove's SDR team.

Most teams lose pipeline not on bad targeting but on follow-up volume, the fifth and sixth touches that reps never get to. That gap quietly costs more meetings than any list problem, and it widens the moment you add new logos faster than you add reps.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three of Prove's top financial-services targets. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them and how the sequencing held up?
email.body3:
Michael, last bit of proof for Prove.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Prove's reply rate likely compares to other funded fintech teams. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Michael, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling SDR output without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem. Right after a raise and a platform launch, ramp and follow-up speed are usually the first things to break, and I get that the timing is busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your team? I will tailor it to Prove either way.
